s: health (state of being in good physical condition and free from illness)
health; soundness; strength; stability (state of being in good condition)
Gesundheit.et: From Middle High German gesuntheit. By surface analysis, gesund (“healthy”) + -heit (“-ness, -hood”). Compare Dutch gezondheid.

s: bless you; gesundheit (response to someone’s sneezing)
Gesundheit.et: From Middle High German gesuntheit. By surface analysis, gesund (“healthy”) + -heit (“-ness, -hood”). Compare Dutch gezondheid.

gestern.et: From Middle High German gestern, from Old High German gesteron, gesteren, from Proto-West Germanic *gesteran. Cognate with English yester, Dutch gisteren.

Geschlechtsverkehr.et: From Geschlecht + -s- + Verkehr. Compare Alemannic German Gschlächtsvercheer, Luxembourgish Geschlechtsverkéier.

s: Der Umsturz des Mutterrechts war die weltgeschichtliche Niederlage des weiblichen Geschlechts.
The overthrow of matriarchy was the world-historic defeat of the female sex.
Geschlecht.et:
From Middle High German geslechte, from Old High German gislahti, a collective formation from slahta, from Proto-Germanic *slahtō, related to *slahaną (“to strike, hit”).
Cognate with Dutch geslacht, Middle Low German geslechte, Italian schiatta, Polish szlach…

s: with a smile on his/her face
Don't give me that look! / Don't make that face!
that which is outward or in front
Es waren viele Leute da, auch einige bekannte Gesichter.
There were a lot of people there, including some more well-known people.
Gesicht.et: From Middle High German gesiht, from Old High German gisiht, from Proto-West Germanic *gasihti. By surface analysis, ge- + Sicht. Cognate with Yiddish געזיכט (gezikht).

s: vision, sight (an observation of an extraordinary or supernatural phenomenon)
1545, Martin Luther, et al. (translators), Biblia, Hans Lufft, Daniel 7:2a
I, Daniel, saw a vision in the night...
Ihr denket das Folgende: ›Dieser junge Schüler ist ein wenig gefährdet, er hat Gesichte, er hat vielleicht zu viel meditiert. […]‹
You think the following: "This young student is rather vulnerable, he has visions, perhaps he has meditated too much. […] "
Gesicht.et: From Middle High German gesiht, from Old High German gisiht, from Proto-West Germanic *gasihti. By surface analysis, ge- + Sicht. Cognate with Yiddish געזיכט (gezikht).

s: Das neue Gebäude nimmt langsam Gestalt an.
The new building is starting to take shape.
shape, build of a person, silhouette, profile
Im Licht der Laterne wurde eine bucklige Gestalt sichtbar.
The hunchbacked shape of a person became visible in the street light.
Der Bahnhofsvorplatz war von finsteren Gestalten bevölkert.
The station forecourt was populated by somber characters.
Auf dem Bahnhof dann, in dem sich senkenden Nebel, ein Gewühl von Pferden und grauen Gestalten, das zuerst unentwirrbar schien und sich dann doch rasch ordnete.
On the station then, in the sinking fog, a crowd of horses and gray characters that initially looked inextricable, but then put itself in order swiftly after all.
Gestalt.et: From Middle High German gestalt, the past participle of stellen (modern stellen, gestellt) used substantively. Cognates include Bavarian Gstoit and Yiddish געשטאַלט (geshtalt).

s: Die eigenen Zimmer hatten sich die Enkel nach persönlichem Geschmack eingerichtet.
The grandchildren had furnished their own rooms according to their personal taste.
Geschmack.et:
From Middle High German smac, from Old High German gismac, gismah, smac from Proto-West Germanic *smakku.
Cognate with Dutch smaak, English smack, smatch, Swedish smak, Danish smag, Yiddish געשמאַק (geshmak).

s: company (presence of other people in general)
I have company. / I'm not alone.
There came a group of people.
society, the public (abstract concept of an organised social group or a local population in general)
Die Gesellschaft besteht nicht aus Individuen, sondern drückt die Summe der Beziehungen, Verhältnisse aus, worin diese Individuen zueinander stehn.
Society does not consist of individuals, but expresses the sum of interrelations, the relations within which these individuals stand.
1932, Erich Mühsam, Die Befreiung der Gesellschaft vom Staat, in: Erich Mühsam: Prosaschriften II, Verlag europäische ideen Berlin (1978), page 253
How do you imagine a society without state and authorities?
society (organised group of people with common interests)
The Goethe Society invites you to a reading.
company, corporation (collection of people and assets with a legal identity, which may or may not be separate from that of its members)
Gesellschaft.et:
From Middle High German gesellescaft, from Old High German giselliscaft. Equivalent to Geselle + -schaft.
Cognate with Dutch gezelschap.

Geschichte.et: From Middle High German geschicht(e) (“event, struggle, story, history”), from Old High German gisciht, from the verb Proto-Germanic *skehaną, whence German geschehen. Unrelated to Schicht. Cognate with Bavarian Gschicht and Vilamovian gyśicht.

s: Gesamtkunstwerk (artistic creation that encompasses music, theatre and the visual arts; a masterpiece)
a dazzling or flashy personality, particularly one who wears extraordinary clothes, piercings, tattoos, etc.
Peters Mutter mit ihrer Federboa und den anstößigen Witzen ist wirklich ein Gesamtkunstwerk.
Peter’s mother with her feather boa and those objectionable jokes is really something else.
a place, scene, or idea, often seemingly chaotic, which is implied to have an underlying beauty
Mein Arbeitszimmer ist keine Müllhalde, das ist ein Gesamtkunstwerk.
My study is not a rubbish dump, it’s a piece of installation art.
Gesamtkunstwerk.et: Compound of gesamt (“whole, total”) + Kunstwerk (“piece of art”).

s: interjection, a particle without an actual meaning, which is used in a conversation
conversation, chat, talk (conversing between people or parties, either for pleasure or for business)
Unsere Unterredung wurde jetzt im leichten Plauderton geführt wie ein harmloses Gespräch unter guten Bekannten.
Our discussion was now held in a light conversational tone like a harmless chat between friendly acquaintances.
Gespräch.et: From Middle High German gespræche, gesprēche, from Old High German gisprāchi, from Proto-Germanic *gasprakją. Cognates with Low German Gespreek, Hunsrik Gesprech, Luxembourgish Gespréich, Dutch gesprek, Old English gesprecan.

Geschoss.et: From Middle High German geschoȥ, Old High German giscoȥ, derivation of the equivalent of schießen (“to shoot”), i.e. "that which is shot (a projectile)". The "floor, story" sense follows a semantic development "to shoot" > "to shoot up, go up quickly in height…

s: a kind of tax paid by landowners or cities for protection by their sovereign
Geschoss.et: ge- + Schoss m, the latter being something shot (√ schießen) and later also something zugeschossen according to modern terminology and hence this tax.

Geselle.et: From Middle High German geselle, from Old High German gisello, gisellio, from Proto-Germanic *gasaljô.

s: law, legal act, bill, statute: a bill by the parliamentary legislator according to the procedures devised in the state’s constitution
law, legal act, bill, statute: any formally published legal norm, a regulation affecting anyone in an unlimited number of cases
law, legal act, bill, statute: a principle governing the phenomena in a particular field of science, a law of nature
Gesetz.et: From Middle High German gesetze, gesetzede, from Old High German gisezzida (“fixing, determination, assessment”), from sezzen (“to make sit, set, put”), from Proto-West Germanic *sattjan (“to set, put down”).

gesund.et: From Middle High German gesunt, from Old High German gisunt, from Proto-West Germanic *gasund, a prefixed form of *sund, from Proto-Germanic *sundaz. Cognates include Bavarian gsund, Alemannic German gsund, Dutch gezond, English sound.

s: Dein Wille geschehe, wie im Himmel so auf Erden.
Thy will be done on earth as it is in Heaven. (Lord's Prayer)
to serve right, to be deserved [with dative ‘someone’ and recht ‘right’] (in this construction passieren is not possible)

geschehen.et: From Middle High German geschehen, geschēn, geschegen, from Old High German giskehan, scehan, from Proto-West Germanic *skehan (“to spring, come up, emerge, happen”). Cognate to Bavarian gschehn and Dutch geschieden.

s: over, lost, done for, doomed, dead
geschehen.et: From Middle High German geschehen, geschēn, geschegen, from Old High German giskehan, scehan, from Proto-West Germanic *skehan (“to spring, come up, emerge, happen”). Cognate to Bavarian gschehn and Dutch geschieden.

s: Mit Hilfe eines geschickten Marketings wuchs das Unternehmen schnell.
The company grew rapidly with the help of some clever marketing.
geschickt.et: From Middle High German geschicket (“arranged, prepared, ready, suitable”), synchronically analyzable as the past participle of schicken.
From Middle High German geschicket (“arranged, prepared, ready, suitable”), synchronically analyzable as the past participle of schicken.

Gestapo.et: Contraction of Geheime Staatspolizei (“secret state police”). The predominant pronunciation with /st/ is from reading out the form as one word and thus to some extent a spelling pronunciation.

s: Ein Gespenst geht um in Europa – das Gespenst des Kommunismus.
A spectre is haunting Europe — the spectre of Communism.
Gespenst.et: From Middle High German gespenst, gespenste, from Old High German gispensti (“temptation, (devilish) illusion”), from spanan (“to lure, to attract”), with ghosts interpreted as "illusions that lure one away"; see the related spannen (“to stretch, span”) for fu…

Gesetzesbrecher.et: From Gesetz (“law”) + brechen (“to break”) + -er, literally “law breaker”.

Geschirr.et: From Middle High German geschirre (“harness, gear”), from Old High German giskirri, giscirri (literally “the trimmed (thing)”), from skeran (“to shear”), from Proto-Germanic *skeraną. Cognate with Alemannic German Geschirr.

s: to confess, to admit (to a mistake, misdeed, something embarrassing); to make known
I confess my love to you.
Mein Mann hat gestanden, dass er eine Affäre hatte.
My husband admitted he had an affair.

Geschenk.et: From Middle High German geschenke, equivalent to ge- + schenken.

s: managing director (male or of unspecified gender)
Mein Busen fängt mir an zu brennen! Entfernen wir uns nur geschwind!
I feel a burning starting in my breast! Let us be off posthaste!
Sag mir, wo die Blumen sind / Mädchen pflückten sie geschwind
Tell me, where the flowers are / Girls have picked them swiftly
geschwind.et: From Middle High German swinde, from Old High German *swind, from Proto-West Germanic *swinþ. See English swith.

Gestank.et: From Middle High German gestanc, from Old High German gistank.

s: Auf deutschen Autobahnen gibt es keine allgemeine Geschwindigkeitsbegrenzung.
On German motorways, there is no general speed limit.
Geschwindigkeitsbegrenzung.et: From Geschwindigkeit (“speed, pace, velocity”) + -s- + Begrenzung (“limit, demarcation”).

s: to form, to shape, to create
to organise, to structure, to arrange

Gesäß.et: From Middle High German gesæȥe, geseȥȥe, gesetze, gesōȥe, from Old High German gisāȥi (“seat, residence, camp, backside”), from "where one sits on"; compare German sitzen. Possibly ultimately from a Proto-Germanic *sētiją. Compare also English seat, Icelandic …

s: shop, store (establishment that sells goods or services to the public; originally only a physical location, but now a virtual establishment as well)
An gut 100 Ständen präsentieren sich Vereine und Geschäfte, bieten die heimischen Gastronomen eine Auswahl ihrer Spezialitäten an.
At around 100 vendor booths you get associations and businesses presenting themselves and local restaurateurs offer their choice delicacies.
Unternehmen und Manager, die bei ihren Geschäften im Ausland Menschenrechte verletzen, sollen künftig auch nach deutschem Zivil- und Wirtschaftsrecht haftbar gemacht werden.
Entrepreneurs and managers that violate human rights during their foreign business activities are to be held liable according to German civil and commercial law in the future.
Geschäft.et: From Middle High German gescheft, from Old High German giscaft, from Proto-West Germanic *gaskafti. Cognate with Yiddish געשעפֿט (gesheft).

s: 1924, Friedrich Bernhard Störzner, Das Torfgespenst, in: Reinhardtswalder Sagenbüchlein, Buchhandlung Otto Schmidt, page 17
At the peat banks it is uncanny at some times. Here, in dark nights, ghostly bluish lights scurry to and fro, who already scared and misguided many a walker.
section of an epic poem; canto
Gesang.et: From Middle High German gesanc, from Old High German [Term?]. By Surface analysis ge- + singen.

s: no use crying over spilt milk, what's done is done
geschehen ist geschehen.et: Literally, “happened is happened”. Compare the English snowclone X is X.

s: Man kann den Zug nicht verlangsamen, geschweige denn anhalten.
You can't slow down the train, let alone stop it.
let alone; used after a negative or limiting clause to introduce another that applies even less
let alone; used after an affirmative clause to introduce another that applies even more
geschweige.et: First-person singular indicative present of geschweigen (“to be silent”) (from Middle High German geswîgen, from Old High German giswîgên), which has been obsolete at least since the 18th century.

Geschwür.et: From Middle High German geswër (“abscess”). Related to Russian хворь.

s: Die gefällige Wohnung in einem ruhigen Bergstädtchen zieht uns an, und wir fassen den Entschluß, den ganzen Tag hier zuzubringen. Da mag denn vor allen Dingen von gestrigen Ereignissen die Rede sein.
The charming flat in a quiet mountain village attracts us, and we decide to spend the whole day here. Yesterday's events are the primary topic of conversation.
Hühner laufen umher, spindeldürre Hunde schnüffeln neugierig herum. Neben einer Schubkarre liegen die Melonen der gestrigen Ernte.
Chickens are running loose, and skinny dogs are sniffing around curiously. The harvested melons from yesterday have been placed next to a wheelbarrow.
Gestrig, aber geil [title, BMW M2 Coupe review]
gestrig.et: From Middle High German gesteric, from Old High German gesterīg. By surface analysis, gestern + -ig.

gesamt.et: From Middle High German gesamt, gesament, from Old High German gisamanōt, from samanōn (“to gather, collect”), from Proto-West Germanic *samnōn, from Proto-Germanic *samnōną (“to bring together”).

Gestade.et: From Middle High German gestade, gestat, from Old High German stad, stado, from Proto-Germanic *staþaz. Cognate with English stathe and Bavarian Gstättn (see also Gstätten).

s: Er ist nicht exzentrisch, sondern gestört.
hands, farmhands, (domestic) servants, domestics, the menial staff
Gesinde.et: From Middle High German gesinde, from Old High German gasindi, gisindi, gisindo, from Proto-Germanic *gasinþiją, from the root *senþ-, sinþ- "to go, travel; seek, aim", from Proto-Indo-European *sent- (“to head for, go”). More at sīþ, *sandijaną. A neuter coll…

s: flavour enhancer (a substance added to a food product to enhance its taste)
Ich mag kein chinesisches Essen, denn es ist voll von Geschmacksverstärkern.
I do not like chinese food because it is full of flavour enhancer.
confession (open admittance of having done something)

Geschwister.et: From Middle High German geswister, from Old High German giswëstar, equivalent to ge- + Schwester. Compare Old Saxon gisustrōni (“sibling”), Old Frisian swesterne, susterne, sisterne (“siblings”), Old English ġesweostren (“maternal cousin, sister”).

s: … die Stämme der Bäume, gescheckt vom Morgenlicht, …
… the stems of the trees, checkered by the morning light, …
interlocutor, collocutor (male or of unspecified gender) (A person who takes part in a dialogue or conversation)
Gesprächspartner.et: Gespräch (“conversation”) + -s- + Partner (“partner”). Cognate with Dutch gesprekspartner.

gesprächig.et: From Middle High German gespræchec, from Old High German gisprāhhīg. By surface analysis, Gespräch + -ig.

Gesine.et: Elaborated form of Gesa, from a German Low German diminutive of Gertrud.

s: Die Zeitung ist auf ein gestelltes Video reingefallen.
The newspaper fell for a staged video.

geschmeidig.et: From Middle High German gesmīdec (“easy to forge or work”), related to schmieden.

s: dexterity (skill in performing tasks, especially with the hands)
nonsense, gibberish (speech or writing that is meaningless, or pointless and vague)
Dann verkünden viele Abgeordnete mit Gemurre im Saal, vor allem aber mit Tweets ihr Entsetzen. Von „sinnfreiem Geschwafel“ schreibt zum Beispiel der Linke Niklas Schrader.
what is happening, what is going on
Nach dem Sturz konnte sie sich an das Geschehen nicht mehr erinnern.
After the fall, she couldn't remember what had happened.
Der Zerfall des Römerreiches raubte der Stadt Rom die alte Stellung als Mittelpunkt alles Geschehens.
The decay of the Roman empire robbed the city of Rome of the old position as the center of all that was happening.
Das sportliche Geschehen während der Weltmeisterschaften wurde von vielen Journalisten verfolgt.
The sporting events during the world championships were followed by many journalists.
sex organ (organ used in sexual reproduction)
Rund eine Million beschriebene Insektenarten leben auf der Erde, Fachleute schätzen die Gesamtzahl aller Insekten auf eine Trillion, das ist eine 1 mit 18 Nullen.
Approximately one million documented insect species live on Earth, experts estimate the total number of all insects at one quintillion, that is a 1 with 18 zeros.
rock, mass of stone, especially as part of the crust of the earth
Viele Gewässer sind mit Quecksilber belastet, das die Goldsucher einsetzen, um das Metall vom Gestein zu lösen.
Many waters are polluted with mercury, which is used by gold diggers to separate the metal from the rock.
Gestein.et:
From Middle High German gesteine, from Old High German gisteini, a collective formation equivalent to ge- + Stein.
Compare Dutch gesteente.

gespalten.et: From Middle High German gespalten, from Old High German gispaltan. Equivalent to ge- + spalten.

Gestirn.et: From Middle High German gestirn, gestirne, from Old High German gistirni. By surface analysis, ge- (collective prefix) + Stern (“star”).

s: rustling, whispering, whistling (weak continuous sound, especially caused by natural phenomena such as wind)
Inmitten grün’ und klaren, seichten Wogen, / Unter wiegend’ Seegras, im Gesträuch tief verborgen, / Wo lehmig’ Kies zum Grund des Sees niedergeht, / Des im Wasser Herrschend’ Reich besteht.

Amidst green and clear, shallow waves, / Under swaying seaweed, deeply hidden in the shrubbery, / Where loamy gravel sinks down to the ground of the lake, / There is the realm of him who rules in the water.
Gesträuch.et: From Middle High German gestriuche. By surface analysis, ge- + Strauch.

s: Zwar bin ich geſcheidter als alle die Laffen, / Doctoren, Magiſter, Schreiber und Pfaffen.
Although I am cleverer than all the poseurs – doctors, masters, scribes and preachers.
Junger Mann, was ist an dir schon dran? / Ich bin sehr gescheit! / Junger Mann, darauf kommt's gar nicht an, nein Ich verzicht', du bist es nicht!
gescheit.et: From Middle High German geschīde (“sensible, sly”), derived from schīden. Related to scheiden (“to separate, distinguish”). Based on the notion of “prudent, circumspect” it was associated with scheuen (“to shun, shy away”) and therefore frequently spelt gesche…

s: German economist and entrepreneur Silvio Gesell (1862–1930)
forget it, forget about it, nevermind, that’s not so problematic, (also in the sense of) that’s one thing, that’s not the worst part
„Ach, jetzt steht mein Name hier zuerst. Eigentlich müssten Sie ja...“ – „Geschenkt!“
“Oh, somehow my name is mentioned first now. Normally you should...” – “Forget about it!”
Dass Sie sich unabgesprochen mit der Konkurrenz getroffen haben – geschenkt! Aber dass Sie dabei Interna ausgeplaudert haben, hat ein Nachspiel.
That you met with our competitors without authority – forget about it! But your disclosing internal information at that meeting will have consequences.
geschenkt.et: The interjection is to be understood as “I cancel whatever moral debt there may be”.

s: curious, excited (of a person; about seeing how something will turn out)
Ich bin gespannt, wie er das lösen wird.
I'm curious to see how he will solve that.
Wenn hier geraucht wird, dann genussvoll, nicht gestresst. Bourgeois liegt die Zigarette zwischen Zeige- und Mittelfinger, vielleicht ist Catherine Deneuve-mäßig der Arm angewinkelt.

s: business climate, business sentiment (the current mood and future expectations of companies regarding their economic situation, often measured by surveys)
Das deutsche Geschäftsklima hat sich im vergangenen Monat überraschend aufgehellt.
German business sentiment brightened unexpectedly last month.
business situation, current business conditions (the assessment of a company's current economic state, especially regarding sales, orders, and profit)
Trotz hoher Energiepreise bewerten viele Unternehmen ihre aktuelle Geschäftslage weiterhin als stabil.
Despite high energy prices, many companies still assess their current business situation as stable.
business expense (a cost incurred in the ordinary course of business, typically tax-deductible)
Die Reisekosten für die Fachmesse gelten als steuerlich absetzbare Geschäftsausgabe.
The travel expenses for the trade fair are considered a tax-deductible business expense.
Jede höhere Geschäftsausgabe muss vom Abteilungsleiter genehmigt werden.
Every major business expense must be approved by the department head.
total turnover, total revenue (the sum of all sales of goods and services of a company or a market within a specific period)
Der Gesamtumsatz des Konzerns stieg im Vergleich zum Vorjahr um fünf Prozent.
The group's total turnover increased by five percent compared to the previous year.
Zur Berechnung des Marktanteils wird der Eigenumsatz ins Verhältnis zum Gesamtumsatz der Branche gesetzt.
To calculate market share, your own sales are related to the total revenue of the industry.
return on assets, return on investment, ROA (a financial ratio that measures the profitability of a company in relation to its total assets, including both equity and debt)
Die Gesamtkapitalrendite gibt Aufschluss darüber, wie effizient das gesamte im Unternehmen arbeitende Kapital eingesetzt wird.
The return on assets provides information on how efficiently the total capital working in the company is being used.
Um den Leverage-Effekt beurteilen zu können, muss man die Gesamtkapitalrendite mit dem Fremdkapitalzins vergleichen.
In order to assess the leverage effect, one must compare the return on assets with the cost of debt.
total amount, grand total, sum of all individual amounts
Der Gesamtbetrag der Rechnung ist sofort fällig.
The total amount of the invoice is due immediately.
Der Bereich, den sich die De­mo­kra­t*in­nen herausgesucht haben, betrifft Millionen US-Amerikaner*innen, deren Gesundheitsversicherung in den nächsten Jahren teurer wird oder ganz wegfällt.
Gesundheitsversicherung.et: Gesundheit + -s- + Versicherung, perhaps a calque of English health insurance.

Gesichtsvorsprung.et:
From Gesicht + Vorsprung.
Coined by German poet Philipp von Zesen in the 17th century.
